transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-10-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Sam Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (ParcelFlow - Product), Jordan Lee (ParcelFlow - Eng), Priya Singh (ParcelFlow - Head of Data)

Summary:
Quick hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + reranking for ParcelFlow search relevance. Demo showed API calls, Redwood Console view, and Optimize suggestions (batching / quantization). Customer asked about latency vs cost, data residency, SOC2/KMS, and pilot scope. Agreed next steps: send pricing/TCO, share demo notebook, customer to provide sample dataset for a one-week pilot.

Topics:
- embeddings index patterns and dimensionality
- rerank endpoint usage and scoring tradeoffs
- Redwood Console: per-route metrics and rerank visualizations
- Optimize: batching, caching, quantization recommendations
- security: SOC2, SSO, VPC, KMS, retention

Action items (brief): see metadata action_items list above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Alex, AE on the account, and Sam is our solutions engineer. Today we'll do a short hosted API demo focusing on embeddings plus our rerank endpoint, show the console, and then leave time for Q&A.
[00:12] Maya (ParcelFlow): Hi, thanks. We're mostly interested in improving search relevance in our internal parcel tracking and documentation search, and also control cost since queries are super high volume.
[00:22] Sam (Redwood): Great, we'll show a simple flow: generate embeddings for docs and queries, upsert into a vector store (we'll demo a minimal Pinecone-style flow), then call Redwood's rerank endpoint which takes top-N candidates and returns a scored reorder. We'll show both the API and Console.
[00:38] Jordan (ParcelFlow): Couple of quick context points — our search traffic is spiky around 9am PST, average query length is ~12 tokens, doc lengths vary but often ~200 tokens. We currently use Elastic for keyword search and Pinecone for vectors. Looking to reduce false positives and improve first-result precision.
[00:58] Priya (ParcelFlow): Security is a requirement — SOC2, SSO/SAML, and we need to understand VPC/on-prem options for sensitive datasets. Also KMS integration for keys.
[01:12] Alex (Redwood): Noted. We have SOC2 and ISO packs, SSO via SAML/Okta, and for regulated flows we offer Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem); for hosted we support customer-managed KMS and audit logs. We'll share the security pack after this call.
[01:30] Sam (Redwood): Jumping into the demo — first the embeddings API. Here's a simple curl:
curl "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"rw-emb-large","input":"How long will my parcel take?"}'
This returns a vector — we typically use 768 or 1024 dims depending on model.
[02:05] [screen share starts] Sam: Now the Console — per-route metrics, token cost, and an embeddings dashboard. You can see recent calls, latency percentiles, and cost breakdown by model. For rerank we show candidate recall and post-rerank precision graphs.
[02:35] Maya: That precision graph is helpful. How do you compute the rerank score?
[02:42] Sam: Good question. The rerank endpoint accepts N candidate doc ids + their embeddings or raw text; we then run a context-aware ranker (ours is a lightweight transformer tuned for relevance) that scores and returns a probability-like score. You can configure candidate window size (N) and model size. Smaller N reduces latency and cost but can miss distant relevant docs.
[03:10] Jordan: So pipeline would be: 1) vector similarity to get top 50, 2) rerank those 50, and 3) return top 5 to user?
[03:18] Sam: Exactly. Typical patterns are top-K retrieval at the vector store layer (K=50 or 100), then rerank top-10 or top-20. For high-QPS workloads we recommend smaller K and more aggressive shortlist heuristics.
[03:35] Maya: What's the latency impact for rerank per call?
[03:40] Sam: On our hosted fleet with rw-rerank-small you can expect median latency around 40-80ms if you pass only embeddings; if you pass raw text it does extra encoding so maybe 70-120ms. For large models or large N it goes up. These are ballpark — we'll run a benchmark with your dataset.
[03:58] Alex: Important tradeoff: you can use embedded-only rerank (cheaper) vs text + cross-encoder (higher quality, higher cost). Cost delta is roughly 2–5x depending on model size and candidate window.
[04:15] Priya: For PII, can you avoid sending raw text to hosted endpoints?
[04:20] Sam: You can send only embeddings from your network — compute embeddings in your environment and send vectors, so raw content never hits Redwood. We also support Private deployment. Note that embeddings themselves can sometimes leak info, so key management and retention settings matter.
[04:40] Maya: Can you show an example rerank request?
[04:45] Sam: Sure — here's a simplified example:
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank
{
  "model":"rw-rerank-small",
  "query_embedding": [ ... ],
  "candidate_embeddings": [[...],[...],[...]],
  "candidate_ids": ["id1","id2","id3"],
  "k": 5
}
Response returns scores and ordered ids. We also include explainability tokens if you enable scoring highlights (useful for debugging).
[05:30] Maya: That explainability would be great for product to show why results changed.
[05:34] Sam: Yep — there's a per-route flag in the Console to enable highlight deltas and token-level attribution.
[05:45] [06:00] Alex: Quick digression on cost controls — Redwood Optimize will suggest batching settings, prefix caching and quantization profiles. For embeddings-heavy workloads Optimize might recommend sequence-length aware batching and quantizing embeddings to 16-bit or 8-bit if appropriate.
[06:18] Jordan: When you say quantization, do you mean you can quantize embeddings? We currently quantize model weights but embeddings as vectors — curious.
[06:28] Sam: Sorry, bit of jargon slip — we mean quantized execution for model inference (weight quantization) to reduce token cost; for embeddings we support lower-dim/approximate indexing like PQ/LSH at the index level. Our recommendation engine will give you a profile: e.g., use rw-emb-small for high-QPS cheap embedding and use PQ on the vector store.
[06:52] Maya: In your Console, can we see per-customer or per-route retention and redaction settings?
[06:58] Alex: Yes, Console has route-level controls for retention, redaction, and audit logs. For Hosted API customers we provide per-token audit trails and can integrate with your SIEM. For Private/Prem we ship with customer-managed logging.
[07:16] Priya: KMS integration — we use AWS KMS, can that integrate?
[07:20] Alex: Yes, we support AWS KMS and HSM for key wrapping. For hosted we offer envelope encryption; for Private you bring your own KMS. We'll include the integration notes.
[07:32] [07:50] Sam (switching back to demo): Now I'll show a small end-to-end: ingest a doc, compute embeddings, do a nearest neighbor query (we'll simulate a Pinecone/Annoy stage), then call rerank to reorder.
[08:05] [screen: code] Sam: Example upsert snippet:
POST /v1/embeddings/upsert
{ "namespace":"parcel-docs", "items":[{"id":"123","embedding":[...],"metadata":{"title":"Delivery SLA"}}] }
Then we query top 100 for a sample query and pass the top 20 embeddings to rerank.
[08:35] Jordan: How do you recommend handling versioning of embeddings and models? We need reproducible search behavior across releases.
[08:42] Sam: We recommend pinning model versions (we support model version tags) and storing embedding vectors with a model_version tag in your vector store. Console can show model versions used per route and we have hooks to roll back to previous embeddings if you run a retest.
[09:02] Maya: For our pilot we probably want hosted to start quickly then evaluate Dedicated if latency/TCO needs it. How does Dedicated differ for rerank?
[09:12] Alex: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, and lower per-token cost at scale. You get isolated capacity and can tune autoscaling/burst policies. For rerank, Dedicated yields lower p95 latencies and more consistent throughput during spikes.
[09:28] Priya: Any minimum commitments for Dedicated?
[09:31] Alex: Yes, Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly or annual commits; we'll include TCO scenarios in the pricing doc. For pilots hosted is usually fine.
[09:40] [10:00] Sam: A couple of product gotchas we've seen — if you send both raw text and embeddings you'll pay for encoding plus rerank compute; so for cost sensitive flows compute embeddings client-side. Also watch candidate window size and batch your rerank requests where possible — our runtime supports multiplexing to amortize overhead.
[10:25] Jordan: Multiplexing?
[10:28] Sam: Continuous batching / multiplexing — the runtime groups small requests to improve GPU utilization; this reduces cost per request at the expense of a tiny added latency (few ms). Optimize gives suggestions for batch size thresholds based on your traffic shape.
[10:45] Maya: Do you have any out-of-the-box connectors for our stack? We run Elastic + S3.
[10:51] Alex: We have reference connectors for Elastic and an S3 ingestion script. For vector stores we provide example integrations with Pinecone, Weaviate, and Open-source FAISS setups. We'll share links to the repo.
[11:05] Maya: Can you share the benchmark template you use so we can plug in our numbers?
[11:10] Alex: Yes — we'll send a benchmark sheet. It includes columns for doc count, avg doc length, query QPS, candidate K, and target p95 latency. Sam will fill in sample numbers after we get your dataset.
[11:22] [11:40] Priya: On compliance: retention windows and deletion are critical. Can you delete vectors on request and provide proof?
[11:46] Alex: We support delete-by-id and TTLs. For hosted we also provide audit logs and deletion receipts. For Private we can run a scrub job and provide attestations as part of the enterprise pack.
[12:05] Jordan: Any known limits on candidate size? Like we can't reasonably send 1k candidates to rerank?
[12:12] Sam: You can technically, but cost and latency scale linearly with candidate count. Typical best practice is keep rerank window under 100 and prune with heuristics before reranking. For extreme cases we offer cascade reranking (two-stage rerank).
[12:30] Maya: Can Optimize automatically suggest PQ or HNSW parameters?
[12:34] Sam: It gives suggestions based on your distribution: e.g., choose HNSW for recall-sensitive workloads, PQ for storage-constrained setups. Recommendations are in the Console Optimize tab.
[12:48] [13:00] Alex: Let's talk success criteria for the pilot — what metric moves the needle for you?
[13:06] Maya: First-result precision and mean reciprocal rank; also a clear drop in user support tickets tied to search.
[13:12] Priya: We'll want 99% uptime SLA and p95 under 200ms for the pilot queries.
[13:20] Alex: For hosted pilot we'll aim for p95 under 200ms, but we'll validate. For production SLA we can discuss Dedicated.
[13:30] Jordan: Timeline — we can have the dataset ready by Oct 21 and want a pilot start end of October.
[13:35] Alex: Sounds good. We'll plan for a one-week pilot starting week of Oct 27 unless you want sooner.
[13:40] [14:00] Maya: Pricing question — ballpark cost for rerank at 1M queries/month?
[14:06] Alex: Ballpark depends on model choice and candidate window. For rw-rerank-small and client-side embeddings it might be low $Xk/month; using cross-encoder large models could be several X. We'll send a TCO spreadsheet.
[14:22] [15:00] Sam: Quick demo note — there may be small transcription issues in the recording, and some product names get garbled (I sometimes say K-V cash instead of KV cache).
[15:12] Maya: [laughs] we've been there.
[15:18] Alex: Ok wrapping up — recap of next steps: Alex to send pricing/TCO and benchmark sheet, Sam to share notebook + API examples, ParcelFlow to provide dataset and confirm success criteria. We'll schedule a kickoff once dataset is in.
[15:35] Maya: Thanks, this was helpful. Looking forward to the notebook and security docs.
[15:40] Jordan: Thanks everyone.
[15:44] Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links and timelines.
[15:48] End of call.
